companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/(loss)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's own disclosed segment operating profit/loss for Core Local Commerce (food delivery + Instashopping/instant retail + in-store), reported each quarter in HKEX results announcements
companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung back to a RMB5.7bn operating profit in Q2 2026 (+52% YoY) as delivery-service revenue returned to positive growth on more 'prudent' (审慎) subsidy spend; note Dolphin Research flags ~RMB3.5bn of this as a one-off gain from shutting a grocery unit, so underlying profitability is closer to breakeven, not a clean beat.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: China e-commerce (Taobao & Tmall) Group adjusted EBITA, YoY decline explicitly attributed to Taobao Shangou/Ele.me instant-commerce investment
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba's disclosed adjusted EBITA for the Taobao & Tmall / China e-commerce Group segment (covers Taobao, Tmall, Taobao Shangou instant commerce and Ele.me), with management explicitly attributing the YoY decline to instant-commerce subsidy investment each quarter
companies.latest_signal: CEO Jiang Fan said Taobao Shangou has held delivery market share since April 2026 while continuing to optimize unit economics without cutting subsidy intensity; management's own guidance is UE breakeven for Shangou before fiscal 2027 ends and full group EBITA breakeven only around fiscal 2029 — the only one of the three still guiding multi-year losses ahead rather than already at/near breakeven.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_name: New Businesses segment operating loss (JD Takeaway/food delivery + Jingxi + overseas, not broken out standalone)
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed 'New Businesses' segment operating profit/loss, the closest proxy since JD does not report food delivery as a standalone P&L line; management gives qualitative commentary on delivery-specific investment and per-order economics on calls
companies.latest_signal: Management said on the Q2 2026 call that total food-delivery investment fell more than 50% YoY with a marked improvement in per-order P&L ('外卖总投入实现同比减亏超50%的显著改善'); New Businesses losses have now narrowed for three consecutive quarters since peaking in Q3 2025, alongside a sharp segment revenue deceleration (-47.6% YoY) signaling JD is deliberately shrinking order volume/subsidy rather than just improving unit economics on flat volume.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked in Q3 2025 (calendar) across all three platforms and has been decelerating since, reinforced by Beijing's anti-'involution' campaign — the State Council's antitrust/anti-unfair-competition office investigated the sector and SAMR credited the food-delivery subsidy crackdown as one of its '2025 anti-involution' achievements alongside EVs, batteries and solar. Meituan has blinked first and hardest, flipping Core Local Commerce back to an operating profit in Q2 2026 (helped by a one-off gain); JD has cut new-business losses for three straight quarters by deliberately pulling back delivery volume growth; Alibaba's Taobao Shangou/Ele.me drag is decelerating on a YoY basis (-76%→-43%→-40%) but management is alone in explicitly guiding several more years of losses (UE breakeven not until FY2027, group EBITA breakeven ~FY2029), making Alibaba the platform still most willing to absorb pain to defend share.
